title: A quorum outside the replica list
description: A store uses N=3, W=2 and R=2. During a partition, it accepts writes on healthy fallback nodes outside a key's normal replica list, with hints for later handoff. A teammate says R+W>N means reads must still see every acknowledged write. How should you explain the trade-off?

options.text: Sloppy quorums keep writes available, but a read from normal replicas may not overlap the fallback write set.
options.explanation: The overlap argument assumes quorums drawn from the same N replicas. Hints and repair help convergence later; they do not make reads fresh during this partition.

options.text: The inequality proves overlap even when reads and writes use different sets of machines.
options.explanation: Counting quorum sizes alone is not enough. The sets must be drawn from the same replica group for that argument to hold.

options.text: Hinted handoff makes fallback writes visible to every normal replica before the write returns.
options.explanation: Handoff happens when the intended replica recovers. Waiting for all normal replicas would defeat the reason for using fallback nodes.

options.text: Switching from timestamps to vector clocks guarantees fresh reads without changing replica selection.
options.explanation: Vector clocks identify causal and concurrent versions that a read encounters. They cannot reveal a version held only on unreachable fallback nodes.
